state.what_this_is: Outcomes of calling functions of GrapiX's dock model on a small workspace. Some outcomes come from the real code and some from a build with a fault put in on purpose; you are not told which. A tree is written [group: tabs, the tab marked * is showing] or {split side-by-side|stacked weights ...: children}. Judge each case only by its own call, its 'before' and its result.
cases:
Case 1. call: openPanel("from-the-future")
   result: THREW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'singleton')

Case 2. call: openPanel("rundown") in the Editor
   result: REFUSED PANEL_NOT_AVAILABLE: "Rundown belongs to the playout application"; the layout it was given is unchanged

Case 3. call: moveGroup("left" onto itself)
   result: REFUSED INVALID_DOCK_TARGET: "a group cannot be moved onto itself"; the layout it was given is unchanged

Case 4. call: registering a panel that is both a singleton and allows more than one
   result: REFUSED PANEL_REGISTRATION_INVALID: "panel "object-manager" cannot be registered: a panel cannot be both a singleton and allow more than one"

Case 5. call: setSplitWeights(root, [1, 2]) on a split with 3 children
   result: REFUSED INVALID_DOCK_TARGET: "split root has 3 children, not 2 weights"; the layout it was given is unchanged

Case 6. call: registering panel type object-manager twice
   result: accepted

Case 7. call: a saved layout with viewState {"api": {"password": "x"}}
   result: REFUSED LAYOUT_VALIDATION_FAILED: "the layout breaks rule 9: viewState.api.password looks like a password, token or secret, which a layout never keeps"

Case 8. call: closePanelChecked("viewport-1"), a panel registered as not closable
   result: REFUSED PANEL_NOT_CLOSABLE: "Composition cannot be closed. It can be moved to another place, or its group shown at full size."; the layout it was given is unchanged

Case 9. call: movePanel("ghost-1" to the centre of group "left")
   result: REFUSED PANEL_NOT_AVAILABLE: "no open panel is called ghost-1"; the layout it was given is unchanged

Case 10. call: movePanel("viewport-1", beside its own group "viewport-group", left); it is the only panel in that group
   result: NOT REFUSED: it returned {root side-by-side weights 0.2 0.6 0.2: [left: objects-1*, assets-1] {center stacked weights 0.68 0.32: [scene-viewport-group: viewport-1*] [timeline-group: timeline-1*, curves-1]} [right: inspector-1*, bindings-1]} (focus=scene-viewport-group); the layout it was given is unchanged

Case 11. call: openPanel("timeline", a second one asked for) while one is open
   result: NOT REFUSED: it returned {root side-by-side weights 0.2 0.6 0.2: [left: objects-1*, assets-1] {center stacked weights 0.68 0.32: [viewport-group: viewport-1*] [timeline-group: timeline-1*, curves-1]} [right: inspector-1*, bindings-1]} (focus=timeline-group); the layout it was given is unchanged

Case 12. call: a saved layout whose root split has weights 0.9, 0.9, 0.9
   result: REFUSED LAYOUT_VALIDATION_FAILED: "the layout breaks rule 4: the weights of split root do not add up to one"

case1_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 1: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Dropping a panel on the centre of a group adds it as a tab of that group and shows it; the group it left keeps its other tabs.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case2_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 2: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Closing every panel of two groups leaves the remaining groups sharing the room, weights adding up to one.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case3_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 3: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Reopening a closed panel puts it back in the group its registration names, and shows it.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case4_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 4: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: UI state that is only about now (which group is maximised, which has focus) may be kept in the saved workspace if it is optional, validated and never changes the arrangement.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case5_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 5: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Closing the last panel of a group removes the group, and a split left with one child is replaced by that child; weights add up to one.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case6_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 6: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: An author's older four-region layout is migrated as the old page showed it: the left dock, the centre and the right dock side by side with the left dock at 0.19 of the width and the right dock at 0.21 (the centre takes the rest), and the timeline under all three across the whole width; every panel kept exactly once and each tab group keeping its tabs.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case7_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 7: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: A layout from a build that had more panels is not damaged: panels this build cannot show stay where they are and are named, with the reason.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case8_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 8: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: A layout that breaks rules is reported with every broken rule named, by number and in words.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case9_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 9: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Dropping a panel above a group whose parent already runs the same way adds one more child to that parent and takes half of the target's share; the parent's other shares do not change.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case10_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 10: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Dragging a divider far past the end stops where the neighbour reaches its smallest share (0.04), and the two shares still add up to what they did.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case11_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 11: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Showing a panel that is behind another tab brings its tab forward and gives its group focus.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case12_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 12: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Opening a panel that is already open shows it instead of making a second copy.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case13_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 13: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: A panel kind renamed since the layout was saved keeps its place under its new name, and the rename is reported.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case14_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 14: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Dropping a panel on the right side of a group whose parent runs the other way makes a new side-by-side split in the target's place, sharing its room equally.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case2_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 2: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Closing the last panel of a group removes the group, and a split left with one child is replaced by that child; weights add up to one.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case3_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 3: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Dropping a panel on the centre of a group adds it as a tab of that group and shows it; the group it left keeps its other tabs.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case4_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 4: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Showing a panel that is behind another tab brings its tab forward and gives its group focus.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case5_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 5: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Closing every panel of two groups leaves the remaining groups sharing the room, weights adding up to one.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case6_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 6: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Reopening a closed panel puts it back in the group its registration names, and shows it.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case7_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 7: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: An author's older four-region layout is migrated as the old page showed it: the left dock, the centre and the right dock side by side with the left dock at 0.19 of the width and the right dock at 0.21 (the centre takes the rest), and the timeline under all three across the whole width; every panel kept exactly once and each tab group keeping its tabs.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case8_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 8: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Dragging a divider far past the end stops where the neighbour reaches its smallest share (0.04), and the two shares still add up to what they did.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case9_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 9: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Opening a panel that is already open shows it instead of making a second copy.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case10_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 10: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Maximising a group does not change the arrangement, so restoring brings back exactly the same proportions.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case11_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 11: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Dropping a panel above a group whose parent already runs the same way adds one more child to that parent and takes half of the target's share; the parent's other shares do not change.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case12_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 12: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: A layout that breaks rules is reported with every broken rule named, by number and in words.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case13_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 13: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: A layout from a build that had more panels is not damaged: panels this build cannot show stay where they are and are named, with the reason.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.

case14_satisfies_rule.instructions: Case 14: does the result satisfy this rule? RULE: Dropping a panel on the right side of a group whose parent runs the other way makes a new side-by-side split in the target's place, sharing its room equally.

criteria.true: Yes: the result satisfies the rule.
